root_cause: The date picker's keyboard handler (_onKeyChange) does not handle the Tab key (keyCode 9). When the picker is open and the user presses Tab on the bound input field (#checkin), the picker remains open and its focusable day buttons (in DOM order after the input) intercept the tab order, preventing focus from moving to the next form field (#guests).
repair_strategy: Add a case for keyCode 9 (Tab) in the _onKeyChange function that calls self.hide() to close the picker. This applies the 'is-hidden' class (display: none), removing the picker's focusable elements from the tab order, allowing the browser's default Tab behavior to move focus to the next focusable element in the form.
expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can now Tab from the check-in date field to the guests field naturally, per WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order). The date picker no longer traps focus when open, and the tab order follows the visual form order.
functional_risks: Tab and Shift+Tab both close the picker; users cannot Tab into the picker grid (arrow keys are the intended navigation per APG).
If the picker is closed on Tab, any partial keyboard navigation state is reset, which is consistent with standard date picker behavior.
verification_requirements: Pressing Tab on #checkin with picker open moves focus to #guests and closes picker.
Pressing Shift+Tab on #checkin with picker open moves focus to previous focusable element and closes picker.
Arrow keys (Left/Right/Up/Down) still navigate dates within picker when open.
Enter (13) and Escape (27) still blur the field and close picker.
